analysis.text:
Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**
3. Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with reference to the provisions of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, as amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018. **(2 marks)**
4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

claims.text: Gamini Perera was originally allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 by a partition decree in 1985. He gifted it to Suresh Perera in 1986 via Deed of Gift No. 515, reserving a life interest for himself and his wife Vinitha. Upon Gamini's death in 1990 and Vinitha's revocation of her life interest via Deed No. 525 in 1991, Suresh held absolute title. When Suresh died intestate on 10 December 1995, his estate devolved under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance: his spouse Kanthi inherited 1/2 of the estate, and his three children (Samantha, Rakitha, Muditha) inherited the other half equally (1/6 each). When Rakitha died on 2 July 2022 leaving his spouse Ann, mother Kanthi, full-brother Muditha, and half-sister Samantha, his 1/6 share devolved as follows: spouse Ann inherited 1/12; mother Kanthi inherited 1/24; full-brother Muditha inherited 1/48; and half-sister Samantha inherited 1/48. When Muditha died on 5 June 2023 unmarried and childless, his accumulated 9/48 share devolved as follows: surviving mother Kanthi inherited half (9/96) and surviving half-sister Samantha (on the father's side) inherited the other half (9/96).

The shares presently owned by each heir in the property are: Kanthi (surviving mother/spouse) holds 61/96 of the property; Samantha (surviving half-sister/daughter) holds 27/96 (or 9/32) of the property; Ann (widow of Rakitha) holds 8/96 (or 1/12) of the property.

Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, the transfer of title of any land in Sri Lanka to a foreigner is prohibited unless exempted under Section 3. Samantha is a citizen of the USA (a foreigner). However, the supplied extracts do not contain Section 3 or specify whether intestate succession/inheritance of land directly by an individual foreigner is considered a prohibited transfer or is exempted under the Act.

The rules under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance are: Section 22 provides that a surviving spouse inherits half of the intestate's property. Section 23 divides the remaining half in order of descendants, ascendants, and collaterals. Section 24 states that children and remoter descendants are preferent, taking equally per capita, while descendants of a deceased child take per stirpes. Section 25 provides that if descendants fail, the property goes to the parents if both are alive; if only one parent is alive, that parent takes half, and the other half goes to full siblings and half-siblings on the side of the deceased parent (or their issue), but if no siblings survive, the surviving parent takes the whole. Section 26 states that if both parents fail, the property goes to the intestate's full and half-siblings and their issue.

Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**
3. Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with reference to the provisions of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, as amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018. **(2 marks)**
4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

Lease or mortgage 50. (1) If in an interlocutory decree for partition any undivided share of the
of undivided share. land constituting the subject-matter of the partition action in which
 such decree is entered is declared to be subject to a mortgage or lease
 the rights of the mortgagee or of the purchaser of the mortgaged share
 under a mortgage decree, or of the lessee, shall-

 (a) where the partition is otherwise than in accordance with an order
 made under subsection (4) of section 26, be limited to the share
 allotted in such interlocutory decree to the mortgagor or lessor; and

 (b) where the partition is in accordance with an order made under
 subsection (4) of section 26, be limited to so much of the extent of land
 and of any owelty or compensation allotted in the partition action to
 the mortgagor or lessor as the court shall determine.

 (2) If in an interlocutory decree for sale any undivided share of the
 land constituting the subject-matter of the partition action in which
 such decree is entered is declared to be subject to a mortgage or lease,
 the rights of the mortgagee or of the purchaser of the mortgaged share
 under a mortgage decree, or of the lessee, shall be limited to the
 mortgagor's or lessor's share of the net proceeds of the sale of the land.

 (3) If in any interlocutory decree for partition or sale any undivided share
 is declared subject to a usufruct, life interest, trust, right of revocation or
 right of re-transfer, the right of such usufructuary, life interest holder,
 beneficiary or of the person entitled to a right of revocation or of re-
 transfer shall be limited-

 (a) in the case of a partition otherwise than in accordance with
 subsection (4) of section 26, to the divided lot or lots allotted in respect
 of such undivided share; and

 (b) in the case of a partition in accordance with subsection (4) of
 section 26, to so much of the extent of land and of any owelty or
 compensation allotted in respect of such undivided share; and

 (c) in the case of a sale, to the net share of the proceeds of sale, in respect
 of such undivided share.

Stamp duty must generally be paid before or at the time of execution of the instrument. The mode of payment is by affixing adhesive stamps to the required value or using impressed stamps. If this is not practicable, it can be paid to the Commissioner General. For instruments of mortgage or lease, stamp duty can be paid to a prescribed bank prior to, at execution, or within seven days of execution if payment is delayed due to reasons beyond control.

 ownership, shall be in force or avail in law unless -

 executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the

 attested by such notary; and

 (b) the left or right thumb impression of every such executant or where

 relevant deed or instrument, in the presence of such notary public and
 the witnesses:

 Provided however, in the event the signature or the thumb
 impression of any such executant cannot be obtained due to any
 reason, the notary public shall state such reason in the attestation,
 and such executant shall affix any other finger impression or toe
 impression, as the case may be.

 (a) both the transferor and the transferee shall affix their signatures and
 thumb impressions as required by subsection (1):

 Provided however, where the transferee is unable to be present

 any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf,
 who shall comply with the requirements set out in subsection (1):

 Provided further, where the transferee is a corporate body and where
 the Board of Directors of such corporate body is unable to be
 present and execute the deed or instrument, such Board shall
 authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or
 instrument on his behalf, who shall comply with the requirements
 set out in subsection (1).

 (b) if the transferee is a minor, a guardian shall be a competent person to
 act on behalf of the transferee for the purpose of this section.

immovable (1) No sale, purchase, transfer, assignment, or mortgage of land or other
properly to be immovable property, and no promise, bargain, contract, or agreement for

[2, 60 of 1947] Thesawalamai Pre-emption Ordinance, of an intention or proposal to
 sell any undivided share or interest in land held in joint or common
 ownership, shall be in force or avail in law unless -
 (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every
 executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the
 witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same
 time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be
 attested by such notary; and

 (b) the left or right thumb impression of every such executant or where
 both thumbs of such executant are missing, the impression of any other
 finger or the toe impression as the case may be, is affixed above or
 besides the signature to the original, duplicate and the protocol of the
 relevant deed or instrument, in the presence of such notary public and
 the witnesses:

 Provided however, in the event the signature or the thumb
 impression of any such executant cannot be obtained due to any
 reason, the notary public shall state such reason in the attestation,
 and such executant shall affix any other finger impression or toe
 impression, as the case may be.

 (2) In relation to a transfer deed -
 (a) both the transferor and the transferee shall affix their signatures and
 thumb impressions as required by subsection (1):

 Provided however, where the transferee is unable to be present
 and execute the deed or instrument, he shall authorise in writing,
 any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf,
 who shall comply with the requirements set out in subsection (1):

 Provided further, where the transferee is a corporate body and where
 the Board of Directors of such corporate body is unable to be
 present and execute the deed or instrument, such Board shall
 authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or
 instrument on his behalf, who shall comply with the requirements
 set out in subsection (1).

 (b) if the transferee is a minor, a guardian shall be a competent person to
 act on behalf of the transferee for the purpose of this section.

1. How do the requirements under the relevant law apply to the Commissioner of Title Settlement and to what types of land would title be registered? **(4 marks)**
2. Could both the owner and occupier make an application in respect of the land? Can the application be rejected without an inquiry? **(4 marks)**
3. A deed affecting land is executed, but the instrument is not presented for registration within the prescribed period. Is registration mandatory, and what is the legal consequence of non-registration? **(4 marks)**

claims.text: The Commissioner of Title Settlement, upon receiving certified copies of cadastral maps, must publish a Notice in the Gazette calling for claimants of the specified land parcel to submit their claims within a prescribed period. Furthermore, a District Court may, after due inquiry on a reference or appeal, order a Declaration of Title for a whole land parcel or a divided portion not below the prescribed minimum extent.

Registration of an instrument is not mandatory to make it valid, and registration does not cure defects. However, an unregistered instrument executed on or after January 1, 1864, is void against subsequent parties claiming an adverse interest on valuable consideration under a subsequent registered instrument. Fraud or collusion in obtaining the subsequent registered instrument defeats its priority.

Under the relevant law, a caveat may be presented by a person (caveator) who has or claims a right, title, or interest in land, or by their Attorney-at-Law, notary, or attorney. For general instruments, the statute refers to the presenter as 'the person who presented it for registration or his agent' but does not specify further qualifications.

Priority notices. 30. (1) Any person (in this section called a 'transferee') acquiring or
 proposing to acquire for valuable consideration from any other person
 (in this section called the 'transferor') any interest or benefit in any land
 may before the execution of the instrument by the transferor with his
 written consent, or after the execution of the instrument by the
 transferor without such consent, present for registration a notice (in
 this Ordinance called a 'priority notice') of his intention to register the
 instrument.
 (2) If, at any time while a priority notice remains in force, any
 instrument is registered whereby the transferee or a person deriving
 title under him acquires for valuable consideration from the transferor
 or a person deriving title under him any interest or benefit in the land
 described in the priority notice, such instrument shall, for the purposes
 of this Ordinance, be deemed to have been registered at the time of
 registration of the priority notice.

 (3) No instrument executed by the transferor while priority notice
 registered with his written consent remains in force and affecting any
 land described in the priority notice shall, except with the written consent
 of the transferee, be registered while the priority notice remains in
 force.

 (4) The Registrar shall, on receiving a priority notice, register it in the
 same manner as other instruments, but shall retain the notice.

 (5) A priority notice shall remain in force for six weeks from the date
 of registration of the notice, but may at any time before the end of such
 six weeks, before the execution of the instrument by the transferor with
 his written consent, or after the execution of the instrument by the
 transferor without such consent, be renewed by the transferee or a
 person deriving title under him for a further period of six weeks, and if so
 renewed shall remain in force for a further period of six weeks computed
 from the end of the first period of six weeks.
 (6) If an instrument is not registered pursuant to a priority notice while
 the notice remains in force, the priority notice shall be deemed to have
 lapsed and shall have no effect under the provisions of this Ordinance.

 (7) This section shall apply to a decree, order, or will affecting land in
 like manner as it applies to any other instrument, except that a priority
 notice as to a decree, or order may not, except with the leave of the
 court, be lodged before delivery in court of the judgment, and a priority
 notice as to a will may not be lodged until after the death of the
 testator.
